label: Doctor and medicine
rationale: Getting treated: going to the doctor, taking medicine and the medicine working.
mixUps: English 'see' and 'take' pull toward miru and toru, but a doctor visit is byouin ni iku and medicine is drunk, kusuri o nomu. The kiku in kusuri ga kiku (it works) sounds the same as kiku 'hear, ask'.

targets.trap: English 'hospital' sounds serious, but byouin is any clinic: for a cold you still go to the byouin, byouin ni iku. Isha ni iku also works; isha o miru or isha ni au doesn't.
targets.use: The normal way to say 'see a doctor', often as advice: byouin itta hou ga ii yo. Casual speech usually drops ni: byouin itta?
targets.notes: Byouin de mite morau (get it looked at) is the other natural way.

example.romaji: sore, byouin itta hou ga ii yo.
example.ja: それ、病院行った方がいいよ。
example.english: You should get that looked at by a doctor.

examplePolite.romaji: sore, byouin ni itta hou ga ii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: それ、病院に行った方がいいですよ。
examplePolite.english: You should have a doctor look at that.

targets.trap: Not kusuri o toru, which would mean fetching it: medicine is 'drunk', kusuri o nomu, even pills.
targets.use: Used for pills, powders and syrups alike, often as a check: kusuri nonda? (did you take your medicine?).
targets.notes: Eye drops take sasu (megusuri o sasu); cream takes nuru (kusuri o nuru). When it works, the medicine kiku: kono kusuri, yoku kiku (this medicine works well).

example.english: Take your medicine and get to bed early.

examplePolite.romaji: kusuri o nonde, yukkuri yasunde kudasai ne.
examplePolite.ja: 薬を飲んで、ゆっくり休んでくださいね。
examplePolite.english: Take your medicine and get some rest.

targets.verbSense: take effect, work (medicine, air con, a remedy); sounds the same as kiku 'listen, ask'
targets.trap: Not kusuri ga hataraku: medicine 'takes effect', kusuri ga kiku, which sounds just like kiku 'listen'.
partners: eakon (air con: eakon kiitenai = the AC isn't doing anything)
targets.use: Asked after a pill as kusuri kiita? and said as it kicks in, kusuri kiite kita. Ga often drops; when the effect wears off, the medicine kireru (kusuri ga kireta).
targets.notes: Kiku~! is also what people say when wasabi or a strong drink hits.

example.ja: 薬効いてきた。だいぶ楽。
example.english: The medicine's kicking in. I feel much better.

examplePolite.romaji: kusuri ga kiite kimashita. daibu raku ni narimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 薬が効いてきました。だいぶ楽になりました。
examplePolite.english: The medicine is starting to work. I feel much better.

reviewPool.english: understand what something means; (negative) make no sense
the light comes on (tsuiteru = is on)
be late for the train (and so miss it)
the last train is gone (no way home)
